Today 4:18 PM Brisbane:
The construction now produces an executable, error-certified clearance-time window without enumerating reactions. Its verified example still requires an astronomically large encoded population, so this is a theoretical capability, not yet a practical simulator advantage.

I’m packaging the proofs, code and ordinary-method comparisons. The next obstacle is obtaining useful guarantees at realistic sizes.

Today 4:35 PM Brisbane:
The reproducible package is attached. It includes the certified finite-population timing window, a separate proved Gaussian fluctuation limit, and comparisons with ordinary simulation and mean-field methods.

The practical accuracy-and-cost advantage remains unearned. I’m continuing on that gap, keeping the successful constructions and their counterexamples.

Attachment: Astra_Exact_Rate2_Clearance_Window_Weak_CLT_20261101.zip

Today 5:37 PM Brisbane:
One major bottleneck has improved: after the model reaches the admitted activated state, removal now has an explicit five-model-time-unit guarantee instead of an enormous waiting bound.

The remaining work is to prove that the faster predictor reaches that state with all errors and costs paid. I’m not treating this conditional improvement as a completed practical simulator.
